_comment_physics: Large-box dendrite. epsilon = 0.10 gives A_max/A_min = 1.10/0.833 = 1.32; it is above 1/15, where the unregularised equation is ill-posed, so willmore_beta > 0 is required: willmore_beta = 0.153 = |S| l*^2 with S = (1 + eps)(1 - 15 eps) = -0.55 and the corner length l* = 0.528 W0 (docs/THEORY.md section 4.3). delta = 0.65. Seed uses a tanh profile with uniform u = -delta (Karma & Rappel 1998).
_comment_grid: 384^3 = 56.6M cells, box 153.2 W0. At dx = 0.4 the |phi| < 0.9 band of the tanh profile, 2 sqrt(2) atanh(0.9) W0 = 4.16 W0 wide, spans 10.4 cells. Measured on an RTX 4090: the solver allocates 5.70 GiB of GPU memory (108 bytes per cell of fields with willmore_beta > 0, plus 2 MiB), 906 MB per checkpoint, up to 630 MB per .vts.
_comment_time: Euler with the linearly implicit Willmore step. dt = 0.00125 is the largest of the candidates 0.02, 0.01, 0.005, ... (each half the previous) whose time error does not exceed the spatial error of h = 0.4 in the max norm and in the mean, both measured with this configuration's physics in a box of side 50.4 up to t = 15 (docs/THEORY.md section 4.3). The explicit thermal update is stable for dt <= 0.026087 (27-point stencil, h = 0.4, D = 2; docs/THEORY.md section 10.1). max_steps = 160000 (t = 200) is an upper bound: the saturation guard stops the run cleanly when the crystal reaches the walls (measured: step 89600, t = 112; six <100> arms with concave faces between them by then). A step takes 122 ms on an RTX 4090 (median of 200 steps), so the 89600 steps to saturation are 182 minutes of compute at that rate.
_comment_output: VTK every 2000 steps (2.5 time units): 46 frames up to saturation, up to 630 MB each, 21.0 GB in total.
_comment_checkpoint: Checkpoint every 8000 steps (10 time units, 16.3 minutes of compute at 122 ms per step on an RTX 4090). 906 MB per checkpoint, keep_last = 3: 2.7 GB.
_comment_initial: r0 = 10 cells = 4.0 W0, 2.6 times the critical radius R_c = 2*d0/delta = 1.54 W0 = 3.85 cells. The tanh profile has width W0, the planar equilibrium width only where A(n) = 1 (it is W0 A(n), 0.833 to 1.10 W0 at epsilon = 0.10; docs/THEORY.md section 4.3).
